headings.title: SMTO-API-0017 — SMTO couldn't confirm a request from a connected program

html:
SMTO-API-0017 — SMTO couldn't confirm a request from a connected program

GUID: 6059d5a7-274d-4a54-8b47-a6456b1afba8
Slug: integration-handler-unavailable
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • A program connected to SMTO sent it work, but SMTO either wasn't ready to take it or didn't report which request it started. The work may or may not have started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open SMTO in your browser and look in the conversation list for a new conversation or task that matches what the program sent. SMTO may have started the work even though the program didn't get a request ID back.
  2. If you find it, follow it there instead of sending it again. If it's waiting for approval or an answer, respond in that conversation. Sending it again could make SMTO do the same work twice.
  3. If nothing was started, wait until SMTO's startup screen shows Ready or System Health shows nothing under Needs attention, then send the request once more. SMTO turns these requests away while the parts that handle them are still starting.
  4. If this keeps happening while SMTO is fully running, ask the person who manages SMTO to check that its installation is complete and up to date. A fully running SMTO that still can't take these requests points to missing or mismatched parts of the installation.

What success looks like

  • You know whether the first request ran, and a new request returns a request ID and a result.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details, or copy the error from the program's output, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the request, since each copy that gets through may run the work again, and don't remove SMTO's data to clear the error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The integration execute, confirm or clarify route found no callable request handler (HTTP 503), or the handler returned no request_id or child request_id (HTTP 500), so the submission's tracking identity is unknown.

What this means

  • Integration submission lacks a callable handler or the handler returns no request/child-request identifier. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • Integration submission lacks a callable handler or the handler returns no request/child-request identifier.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish an absent handler from a submission that returned no ID after it may have been accepted.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the failing route and confirm the agent request, confirmation and clarification handlers are registered (a partial startup or mismatched installation leaves them unset); reinstall or restart matching components. Before resubmitting, search conversation and task state for work created by the original submission, since a 500 after the handler ran can mean it was accepted.
  • Restore matching application components and preserve this occurrence for investigation. Check whether a request was accepted before resubmitting integration work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Matching components return a valid correlated identity and any earlier acceptance is reconciled before resubmission.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
